content: Typical Overhead Ratios for South African IT Holding Companies (2020-2023) Year Typical Overhead Ratio Benchmark 2020 - 2021 - 2022 - 2023 - Data Source: Google Search Governance Structures: Board, Audit, and Risk Management Frameworks The evaluation of governance structures within Veramani IT Holding Company necessitates a comprehensive analysis of its board composition, audit practices, and risk management frameworks in relation to prevailing industry benchmarks. Boards were often required to include members with expertise in IT and data governance, ensuring that decisions regarding technology investments, risk management, and information security adhered to both ethical and economic standards . A direct comparative analysis, as illustrated in the Governance Framework Comparison between Veramani IT Holding Company and Industry Standards, highlights how the organization benchmarks its board composition against these evolving sector requirements. The King IV Report also emphasized transparency and stakeholder-centric approaches, encouraging organizations to align their governance practices with broader societal needs, particularly amid challenges such as unequal access to technology and systemic socioeconomic disparities . Furthermore, environmental, social, and governance factors emerged as pivotal areas of focus, aligning IT governance with internationally recognized standards to enhance both corporate reputations and long-term resilience [6] . As the corporate landscape progressed toward the King V framework, set to come into force in 2026, anticipatory changes included a sharper focus on artificial intelligence governance and advanced analytics [6] . Risk management frameworks form the final pillar of this governance analysis, where Veramani IT Holding Company is once again benchmarked against rigorous industry standards. Established frameworks such as the NIST Risk Management Framework, ISO 31000, and COSO Enterprise Risk Management remain foundational due to their adaptability and longstanding credibility, serving as the backbone for many organizations managing complex risks . The ISO 31000 and COSO frameworks, known for their general applicability across industries, continue to provide robust guidelines for risk identification, mitigation, and resilience-building, which inherently includes auditing processes .
